name: Lithium
listed_description: Build high performance C++ HTTP servers without being a C++ expert.
reason: Directional claim only. The repo README says 'Lithium HTTP server and SQL drivers are ranked #1 on the TechEmpower benchmark (composite score)' and docs/introduction.md says it is 'benchmarked againts 200+ other frameworks' at TechEmpower; neither gives a figure or a named runner-up. tfb-status.techempower.com and matt-42.github.io (project site) are EGRESS_BLOCKED, the TechEmpower FrameworkBenchmarks entry (frameworks/C++/lithium README and benchmark_config.json) only configures the tests, and the docs directory has no benchmark page. The HN thread by the author (item 24315285) that carries the actual comparison against actix-web and h2o is not reachable from this environment; the catalog already holds a tier B record for it in data/wave5/raw/w5-http-servers-registry.json.

name: lwan
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline reachable. The README Performance section gives absolute figures only (about 320000 requests/second on a Core i7 laptop without disk access, about 290000 for files up to 16 KiB, 185000 for larger files, weighttp on the same machine) and quotes 'For Round 10, Lwan has taken the crown' (TechEmpower) and an InfoQ line without numbers. The TechEmpower Round 10 blog, InfoQ, lwan.ws and tfb-status are EGRESS_BLOCKED; the TechEmpower lwan README and benchmark_config list endpoints but hold no results; the-benchmarker/web-frameworks has no lwan entry; nanoant/WebFrameworkBenchmark has no lwan row; lwan issue search for nginx benchmarks shows no numbers. The catalog already has a tier B record for the Round 10 JSON result in data/wave5/raw/w5-http-servers-gh-cpp.json, taken from an archived copy of the blog that this session could not open.

name: lwIP
reason: No speed comparison found. The README of the GitHub mirror (the listed savannah.nongnu.org page is EGRESS_BLOCKED) states only that the focus is reduced RAM use for systems with 'tens of kilobytes of free RAM and room for around 40 kilobytes of code ROM' and lists a 'raw/native API for enhanced performance', with no numbers and no named competitor. lwIP is the incumbent baseline in other projects' comparisons (see the Mongoose record in w5-mine-d.json), not a challenger.

name: nope.c (WAFer)
listed_description: Ultra-light software platform for scalable server-side and networking applications (think node.js for C programmers).
reason: Directional claim only: the README says WAFer has 'a memory footprint that is only a fraction of that of node.js and other bulky frameworks' with no figures, no benchmark and no methodology. The wiki is empty, the only issue matching 'benchmark' is #51 'Load Test Failed' (2014, no numbers visible), the repo has no benchmark or docs directory, and the /r/programming discussion credited in the README is blocked. Last commit 2017-12-07, GPL-2.0, 698 stars.
